en: The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Epithets of the Great Auspicious Goddess (Mahāśrī-devī).
[Posthumously honored with the titles: Grand Master Opening the Prefecture, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes; Special Advance; Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial;
Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households; conferred purple robes; posthumously appointed as Minister of Works; posthumous title: Da-jian (Great Mirror).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, Possessor of Great and Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Command. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat...
In the world of Sukhāvatī, at that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara approached the place where the Buddha was,
prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvā Mahāśrīdevī also went to where the Buddha was,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
Then the World-Honored One...
Desiring to benefit all sentient beings who are of meager merit and impoverished,
she beheld the goddess Śrī and addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās,
or any other class of sentient beings who know these twelve names of the Great Auspicious Goddess, [they shall attain liberation].
By upholding, reciting, practicing, making offerings to, and explaining it to others,
one can eliminate all karmic obstacles of poverty and attain abundant wealth, treasures, and prosperity.
At that time, all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings in the assembly spoke with one voice, saying:
"What the World-Honored One has spoken is true and not false."
"We wish to hear the twelve names.
We pray only that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion, will expound them.
The Buddha said, "You should listen well."
Now I shall explain for you what are called these twelve names:
Auspicious, Auspiciousness, Lotus, Adorned, Endowed with Wealth, White, Great Renown, Great Radiance, Giver of Food, Giver of Drink, Jewel Light, and Great Fortune.
"You should receive and uphold this.
I shall now further recite these auspicious words:
Tadyathā śrīṇi śrīṇi sarvakalyāṇasādhanī sīni sīni sīni sīni sīni sīni arokṣimaṃ naśyeya svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"This Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī and its twelve names are able to eliminate poverty and all inauspiciousness."
All their aspirations and requests shall be fully accomplished.
If one can recite this sutra three times during the day and night, [this shall come to pass].
Recite this three times at each of the three periods of the day,
or maintain it constantly without interruption.
With a mind intent on benefiting others, offer sincere worship according to one's ability to the Bodhisattva Mahāśrīdevī.
They will swiftly obtain all manner of wealth, abundance, joy, and auspiciousness. At that time,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the great assembly— the eight classes of beings including devas and nāgas—
heard from the Buddha the exposition of the twelve names and the mantra.
They marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
All were filled with great joy;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.

The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Epithets of the Goddess Mahāśrī The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Epithets of the Goddess Mahāśrī: Thus have I heard. At one time the Bhagavān was dwelling in the city of Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and a great assembly of bodhisattvas. At that time, the Bhagavān addressed the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, there is a goddess named Mahāśrī who possesses twelve epithets. If sentient beings hear her name and recite it, they shall obtain immeasurable merit and be freed from all calamities. Listen attentively; I shall now explain them for you. Ānanda replied to the Buddha, saying: "Excellent, World-Honored One! We are eager to hear and receive this teaching. The Buddha said: "The first epithet is 'The Goddess Who Bestows Abundant Wealth. The second is 'The Goddess Who Upholds the Three Jewels. The third is 'The Goddess Who Protects All Sentient Beings. The fourth is 'The Goddess Who Increases Merit and Virtue. The fifth is 'The Goddess Who Eliminates All Suffering. The sixth is 'The Goddess Who Fulfills All Wishes. The seventh is 'The Goddess Who Sustains the World. The eighth is 'The Goddess Who Grants Peace and Security. The ninth is 'The Goddess Who Purifies All Obstacles. The tenth is 'The Goddess Who Increases Longevity. The eleventh is 'The Goddess Who Brings Joy to All. The twelfth is 'The Goddess Whose Name is Universally Honored. "Ānanda, if there are kings, ministers, or commoners who, with a sincere heart, write down these twelve epithets and place them within their homes, or if they recite them morning and evening, they shall be protected by the goddess and never suffer from poverty, nor shall they encounter any misfortune. Furthermore, if there are those who are afflicted by various diseases, or those who are pursued by enemies, or those who face obstacles in their travels, if they hear this name and recite it with single-minded devotion, they shall all be delivered from suffering and attain peace and happiness. "Ānanda, you should know that the power of this goddess’s name is inconceivable. It can cause the rain to fall in due season, the harvests to ripen in abundance, and all living beings to dwell in harmony. Therefore, you should propagate this scripture widely so that all may benefit. Having spoken thus, the Bhagavān rejoiced, and the venerable Ānanda, along with the entire great assembly, having heard the Buddha’s teaching, were overjoyed and faithfully practiced it. The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Epithets of the Goddess Mahāśrī is hereby concluded.
